"Bi-ʿad Iram" (The people of ʿAd, of Iram): it is the first ʿAd.

"Dhat al-ʿimad" (Of the lofty pillars): for the height of a man among them was twelve cubits.

"Jabu al-sakhr bil-wad" (Who hewed the rock in the valley): i.e., they cut the rocks and made houses out of the boulders in the valley of al-Qura.

"Dhi al-awtad" (Of the stakes): i.e., the possessor of stakes, which are four stakes to which the hands and feet of the one being tortured are fastened.

"Taghaw fil-bilad" (Who transgressed in the lands): i.e., they behaved arrogantly therein, wronged the servants, and greatly spread corruption therein.

"Fa-aktharu fiha al-fasad" (And multiplied corruption therein): i.e., shirk and killing.

"Sawta ʿadhab" (A scourge of punishment): i.e., a type of punishment.

"La-bil-mirsad" (Indeed, is in ambush): i.e., He watches the deeds of the servants in order to recompense them for them.

Meaning of the verses:

The Almighty's saying, ﴿By the dawn, and by ten nights, and by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes﴾: these are four things by which Allah the Exalted has sworn. This is because the surah is Meccan and deals with creed, and among the things the polytheists denied most was resurrection and recompense; therefore this response is intended and meant. What confirms it is what the Almighty mentions afterward of the manifestations of His power in the verses that follow, for power is what makes resurrection and recompense possible. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 89, verses 15–20:

Explanation of the words:

Fa-amma al-insan (as for man): i.e., the disbelieving polytheist.

Ibtalahu (He tested him): i.e., He examined him.

Wa akramahu wa na''amahu (and honored him and granted him bounties): i.e., with wealth and standing, and blessed him with good things.

Akramani (He has honored me): i.e., He has favored me, because of my wealth, over others.

Faqadara 'alayhi rizqahu (and restricted his provision): i.e., He constricted it for him and did not widen it for him.

Ahanani (He has humiliated me): i.e., He has disgraced me with poverty, and he did not thank God for what He bestowed upon him of soundness of limbs and bodily well-being.

Kalla (No!): i.e., the matter is not as this disbeliever sees it, believes it, and says.

Al-turath (the inheritance): i.e., the inheritance.

Aklan lamma (devouring greedily): i.e., eating a great deal and grabbing intensely, as they seize the share of women and children and do not give them their inheritance from the estate.

Hubban jamma (boundless love): i.e., intense and abundant love.

The meaning of the verses:

The words of God, Exalted is He, ﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him and honors him and grants him bounties, he says, "My Lord has honored me."﴾ The saying of God, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [Verse 14] has preceded, and it indicates that God, Exalted is He, loves from His servant that he worship Him and thank Him, so that He may honor him in the abode of His honor on the day of meeting Him. God's informing His servants that He is watchful, observing their deeds, clearly shows that He warns them against His disobedience and encourages them to obey Him. From this it is concluded that God, Exalted is He, does not approve of disbelief for His servants, and that He loves for them gratitude. As for man, what does he love and what does he dislike? God, Exalted is He, says about him: ﴿As for man﴾, meaning the polytheist, and most people are polytheists, ﴿when his Lord tests him﴾, i.e., examines him, so He honors him with wealth, children and standing, and grants him bounties with provisions and good things, so that God may see whether he gives thanks or disbelieves. Then he says boastfully, "My Lord has honored me", i.e., He has favored me over others because of the virtues and distinctions I possess that these poor people do not have. ﴿But when He tests him and restricts his provision﴾, i.e., when He tests him and constricts his provision, so that Exalted God may see whether the tested servant endures or becomes distressed, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me", i.e., He has disgraced me by impoverishing me.

And the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿No! Rather, you do not honor the orphan, nor do you urge one another to feed the needy, and you devour the inheritance greedily, and you love wealth with boundless love﴾. That is: Refrain, you materialists who measure all matters by the standards of matter. God, majestic in His majesty, widens provision as a test for the servant, to see whether he gives thanks for God's blessings upon him by mentioning and thanking them through faith and obedience, and He constricts provision as a trial, to see whether the servant endures God's decree or becomes distressed. You materialists only see that widening is honor and constriction is humiliation. No, the matter is not so. This materialist theory of yours came to you from your love of this world and your being deceived by it. The evidence for this is your humiliation of orphans and your failure to honor them because of their weakness and helplessness before you, and your failure to gain material benefit from them. Another proof is that you do not urge yourselves or others to feed the needy, while they are hungry before you. Another is that you devour the inheritance, i.e., the estate, with greedy, intense devouring, gathering the wealth of the heirs, children and women, into your own wealth, and depriving the two weak groups, children and women. And another: ﴿and you love wealth with boundless love﴾, i.e., with strong, intense love. No! Refrain and step out of the circle of this materialist theory before the punishment arrives and what you dislike descends. So believe in God and His Messenger.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The materialist theory is not of recent origin, for the materialists among the polytheists of Quraysh in Makkah knew it fourteen centuries ago.

2- The obligation to honor orphans and to urge the feeding of the hungry among the poor and needy.

3- The obligation to give inheritances to their rightful recipients, whether male or female, young or old.

4- Condemnation of the love of wealth, which leads to withholding rights and weighs matters by its own scale of strength and weakness.

Explanation of the words:

"Wal-malaku saffan saffan" (And the angels in rows, row upon row): That is, the angels, row after row.

"Wa-ji'a yawma'idhin bi-Jahannam" (And Hell is brought on that Day): That is, it is dragged by seventy thousand chains, each chain held by seventy thousand angels.

"Yatadhakkaru al-insanu" (Man will remember): That is, the disbeliever will recall what the messengers said to him of Allah's promise and threat, on the Day of his meeting (with Allah).

"Wa-anna lahu al-dhikra" (But how will remembrance avail him?): That is, remembrance will not benefit him on this Day.

"Qaddamtu li-hayati" (I should have sent ahead for my life): That is, this faith and righteous deeds.

"La yu'adhdhibu 'adhabahu ahad" (None will punish as He punishes): That is, none will punish with a punishment like the punishment of Allah, in its severity and intensity.

"Wa-la yuthiqu wathaqahu ahad" (Nor will anyone bind as He binds): That is, no one will bind with a binding like the binding of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

"Ya ayyatuha al-nafsu al-mutma'innah" (O soul at peace): That is, the believing, secure soul, safe today from the punishment, because the glad tidings of salvation have appeared to it.

"Irji'i ila rabbiki" (Return to your Lord): That is, to His nearness, in the abode of His honor, which is Paradise.

"Fadkhuli fi 'ibadi" (Enter among My servants): That is, among the total of My righteous, God-fearing believing servants.

"Wadkhuli jannati" (And enter My Paradise): That is, the abode of My honor for My friends.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, "When the earth is pounded, pounded" (89:21), are like His words, "And when the earth is stretched out and casts forth what is within it and empties itself" (84:3–4). "And your Lord comes" (89:22), that is, to decide the judgment. "And the angel, rank upon rank" (89:22), row after row. "And Hell is brought on that Day" (89:23), dragged by seventy thousand chains, each chain held by seventy thousand angels, here and on that Day and at that hour. "Man will remember" (89:23), the heedless, the excessive, the one who turns away from the call of the messengers, the one who disbelieves in meeting Allah and in recompense for deeds. "And how will remembrance avail him?" (89:23). Here he remembers, but what does he remember? And his disbelief was wide and his evil was spreading. What does he remember, and will remembrance benefit him? No, by Allah, no. And what could he say in this dreadful situation? He says, regretful and sorrowful, "Would that I had sent ahead for my life" (89:24), that is, this present life that stands before him. And will wishing benefit him? No, by Allah, no.

The Exalted said, informing about the severity of the punishment and the strength of the binding: "So on that Day" (89:25), when the Resurrection occurs, the Lord comes to decide the judgment, Hell is brought, man remembers, regrets and grieves. This is what He alluded to in His words: "So on that Day none will punish as He punishes" (89:25), that is, no one in this world, however much he exaggerates in punishment, punishes like the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. "Nor will anyone bind as He binds" (89:26), that is, no one in this world binds with the binding of Allah in the Hereafter. This is a depiction of Allah's punishment of His enemies, from among the people of polytheism toward Him, disbelief in His signs, His Messenger and meeting Him. As for the people of faith in Him and obedience to Him, who are His friends, those who believed in the world and were God-fearing, behold, they are being called, so listen: "O soul at peace" (89:27), to the true promise and threat of Allah in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger. So it believed and feared God, and it abandoned polytheism and evil, and it was at peace through faith, mindful of Allah, its eye comforted by the love of Allah and His Messenger, and by what the Most Merciful had promised it. "Return to your Lord" (89:28), that is, to His nearness in the abode of His honor, while you are "well-pleased" (89:28), Allah's reward to you being pleasing, and you being pleased with by your Master. "So enter among My servants" (89:29), that is, among the total of My righteous servants. "And enter My Paradise" (89:30). This is said to her when Allah sends the souls back to the bodies on the Day of Return. When she enters, the angels greet her with peace, she is led to the place of assembly, she is given her record in her right hand, and then it is said to her, "Enter among My servants," that is, among their number, "and enter My Paradise," after she has passed over the Sirat.
